acceptance.given: The repository contains the frozen historical files identified by the repository-owned replay receipt before the repair is applied.

oracle.expected: The historical-byte integrity check records the pre-repair SHA-256 values for every declared historical file and, after the repair, verifies the same repository-relative files still exist with identical bytes and SHA-256 values.
forbidden: Any declared historical file is added, removed, renamed, rewritten, or has a post-repair SHA-256 value different from its pre-repair value.
A replay receipt reports success when the historical-byte integrity check is missing, incomplete, or detects a byte mismatch.
oracle.observable: The replay result exposes the declared historical file paths with pre- and post-repair byte identities, and the targeted test passes only when every comparison is identical.

acceptance.then: The repair leaves the declared historical bytes unchanged and reports a successful immutable-byte comparison.
acceptance.when: The repository-owned historical compatibility replay runs after a repair candidate is prepared.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Mutate one declared historical file in an isolated test copy and require the historical-byte integrity check to reject the replay result.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Extend the repository-owned replay receipt and its historical-compatibility test so the declared frozen historical files are byte-compared before and after repair, with any missing file or changed digest preventing success.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: The receipt may add historical-byte integrity fields without changing the existing receipt identity, historical command evidence, or empty authorization semantics.

slice_hint.state_transition: Declared historical files exist with their pre-repair bytes; replay verifies the same paths after repair and either records identical byte identities or terminates unsuccessfully.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The targeted historical compatibility replay succeeds only if every declared historical file remains present at the same repository-relative path with exactly the pre-repair bytes; otherwise it fails.
